note: Second full-tier run, same manifest, tree differing only by the seven shipped-doc fixes. Paired with run 1 this measures detector stability.

discrepancies.claim: The PATH entry is a symlink: install step 9 is headed "PATH entry (`config-change`) — transparent prompt: 'Install `abcd` symlink to `~/.local/bin/abcd`?'", step 8 talks only of symlink resolution, and the `config-change` row lists "PATH symlink" as its example.
discrepancies.reality: Since spc-35/adr-46 the shipped default is an abcd-owned regular-file COPY of the verified release artefact, promoted out of the persistent plugin data dir's cache (`<data-dir>/cache/abcd-<goos>-<arch>`), SHA-256-re-verified on every promotion, with ownership established by a provenance record at `~/.abcd/path-entry` (internal/core/ahoy/owned_copy.go:14-58, apply.go:775-800 `installOwnedEntry`). A pinned symlink is only the loud degradation path when no cache artefact exists, and a plugin-root symlink is now a `symlink.legacy` gap to be healed. `abcd ahoy uninstall --help` says "abcd's owned PATH copy, and its provenance record"; the chapter never mentions the copy, the cache, or the data dir.

discrepancies.claim: Install step 9 quotes a per-entry prompt with a visibility-dependent default: "transparent prompt: 'Install `abcd` symlink to `~/.local/bin/abcd`? Default: yes for private repos, no for public.'"
discrepancies.reality: No such prompt exists anywhere in the binary (no match for that text in internal/). The PATH entry is written under the single `config-change` category-level approval (`stepSymlink`, apply.go:742-750, gated on `a.approved[ConfigChange]`), and nothing keys the decision or its default on repo visibility.

discrepancies.claim: The user-scope tree enumerates exactly `history/`, `config.json` (a later phase) and `memory/` (a later phase).
discrepancies.reality: The shipped binary also writes and reads `~/.abcd/path-entry` — the PATH-entry provenance record, deliberately home-scoped rather than data-dir-scoped (owned_copy.go:43-58) and written/removed by `ahoy install` / `ahoy uninstall` — and `~/.abcd/voyage/<root-sha>/disembark/history.jsonl` (internal/core/lifeboat/voyage.go:59-63). The real `~/.abcd/` on this machine holds `history`, `sources`, `voyage`. None of the three appear in the tree.

discrepancies.claim: Uninstall "removes the marker block and abcd's own `PATH` entry (if owned by this plugin)" and "Leaves the entire `.abcd/` namespace intact … and the history store".
discrepancies.reality: Uninstall also deletes the `~/.abcd/path-entry` provenance record along with the owned copy — the shipped help reads "Remove the marker block, abcd's owned PATH copy, and its provenance record (leaves .abcd/ intact)" (apply.go:1030, 1078-1094). A user-scope `.abcd/` file is removed, which the chapter's "leaves .abcd/ intact" framing does not cover, and the provenance record is never named.

discrepancies.claim: The chapter documents `--bin-dir` only as an install flag (:369); uninstall is described with no flags.
discrepancies.reality: `abcd ahoy uninstall --bin-dir <dir>` ships ("directory holding the PATH entry to remove; needed only when it was installed with --bin-dir into a directory that is not on PATH") and is in the committed surface snapshot .abcd/development/release/surface.json as the sole flag on `abcd ahoy uninstall`.

discrepancies.claim: Bare `/abcd:ahoy` shows "folder kind, plugin-root status, root SHA, binary vintage/staleness, citations on a managed repo, gap count, guard health, and the banlist block" — the same nine fields listed in the architecture table and in the acceptance criterion.
discrepancies.reality: The CLI also renders an `install:` line from `signals.install_mode` whenever it is non-empty — `dev (tip build)` or `pinned`, either possibly carrying ` (shadowed on PATH)` (internal/surface/cli/cli.go:1780-1782). `commands/ahoy.md` instructs the agent to report it ("Report it so a dev install — or an entry abcd wrote that is not the one that runs — is never invisible"), but no enumeration in this chapter names it.

discrepancies.claim: The detection pass is enumerated as twelve steps (0 folder classification … 11 name-banlist scaffolding); the `config-change` and `plugin-owned` category rows (:238-239) enumerate their examples.
discrepancies.reality: The pass also runs a guard-health probe and a citation probe that the list omits. `detectGuardHealth` fills the `guard` envelope key and `detectGuardGaps` emits three real gaps — `guard.hook_missing` and `guard.binary_unreachable` (`plugin-owned`) and `guard.registry_unloadable` (`config-change`) — (detect.go:85-87, guard_health.go:121-148), and `detectCitations` fills `signals.citations` (detect.go:53-57). The bare status board and the JSON envelope both surface guard health, so the chapter names the output while documenting no step that produces it, and the category examples list none of the three guard gaps.

discrepancies.claim: "Every event command is a self-provisioning shim, not a plain binary call: the non-SessionStart shims attempt `hooks/bootstrap.sh` when the plugin-root binary is missing (throttled by a `.bootstrap.attempt` marker within a 10-minute window), then fall back to a PATH-resolved `abcd` before failing loudly."
discrepancies.reality: The shipped `SessionEnd` entry in hooks/hooks.json — a non-SessionStart shim — makes no bootstrap attempt at all: it tries `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/abcd`, then a PATH-resolved `abcd`, then prints "the plugin binary is missing, so this session's transcript was not captured" and exits 1. There is no `bootstrap.sh` call and no `.bootstrap.attempt` marker in that command. Only UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse and PreCompact carry the throttled bootstrap.

discrepancies.claim: "this step only reports which **opt-in** scanners are on PATH: `gitleaks` (deeper secret scan) and `trufflehog` if `scan.deep` is (or would be) enabled."
discrepancies.reality: `detectDependencies` (detect.go:165-182) emits `deps.trufflehog_missing` unconditionally whenever trufflehog is absent from PATH — it reads no config and has no `scan.deep` guard. Only the separate `config.scan_deep` prompt is conditioned on visibility=private plus trufflehog being present (detect.go:349-353).

discrepancies.claim: "Each detected discrepancy becomes a **gap** with a stable `id`, a `category`, a `scope`, a `title`, `detail`, and a `fix_hint`."
discrepancies.reality: The shipped `Gap` carries two further fields the chapter itself depends on elsewhere: `required` and `resolvable` (visible in every `abcd ahoy dry-run` gap object; the "zero actionable gaps" contract at :380-383 and :467-469 is defined as required-and-resolvable). The enumerated gap shape is one field pair short of what ships.

discrepancies.claim: The chapter describes the four synthesis sub-verbs as "deterministic-or-validate-host-JSON" and § 7 says bare invocation prints "the available sub-verbs ... and flags only", but the chapter never names a single flag. No flag appears anywhere in the file.
discrepancies.reality: Four host-JSON flags ship: `disembark graveyard --lessons-json <file|->`, `disembark review --review-json`, `disembark press-release --press-release-json`, `disembark principles --principles-json` (all confirmed in `--help` and in the committed snapshot `.abcd/development/release/surface.json`). `--lessons-json` is REQUIRED: `abcd disembark graveyard <lifeboat-dir>` exits with `--lessons-json <file|-> is required`, so a reader working from this chapter alone cannot run the graveyard sub-verb at all. `commands/disembark.md` documents all four.

discrepancies.claim: Acceptance: "Given a corpus repo with an intent corpus, ADRs, and a memory backend present, when `/abcd:disembark pack <source-repo> <dest>` runs to completion, then `<dest>` contains all sections in § 5 and the review returns a registered verdict of `SHIP`."
discrepancies.reality: Packing abcd's own repository — the reference corpus repo, with intents, ADRs and the memory backend all present — never runs to completion: `abcd disembark pack . <dest>` exits 1 with `4 hard-fail secret(s) in planned content (first: activity/issues/resolved/iss-307-scanner-network-ipv4re-and-macre-rely-on.md (net:mac))`. The hits are prose about MAC/IPv4 regexes in committed issue records, i.e. scanner false positives. `disembark plan` on the same tree succeeds, so the criterion is unreachable on the repo it is written for and the § 7 pack/review acceptance has never been exercised end to end here.

discrepancies.claim: The DESTINATION SAFETY GATE is described as "refuse unless <dest> is absent, empty, or carries a parseable _provenance.json", and § 7's gate bullet (line 124) enumerates the same three conditions plus the source-overlap rule at line 118.
discrepancies.reality: `checkDestination` in internal/core/lifeboat/pack.go:130-176 refuses on three further conditions the chapter never states: a symlinked destination (`destination %s is a symlink; refusing`), a destination inside a `.git` directory (`destination is inside a .git directory; refusing`), and a destination that exists but is not a real directory (`destination exists and is not a real directory; refusing`). It also resolves symlinks before the overlap check, so a destination reached through a symlinked parent is caught — none of that is in the record. `commands/disembark.md:71` does mention the symlink refusal.

discrepancies.claim: § 5 "Output shape" is presented as the complete layout, closing with "The synthesis sub-verbs add the rest over an already-packed lifeboat: `press-release` writes `press-release.{json,md}`, `principles` writes `principles.{json,md}`, `review` writes the verdict artefact, and `graveyard` validates and writes the lesson JSON." No path is given for the review or graveyard outputs, and neither appears in the tree.
discrepancies.reality: Verified by running the synthesis verbs over a packed lifeboat: `review` writes `review/review-<manifest-prefix>.json` AND `review/review-<manifest-prefix>.md` — a whole top-level `review/` directory absent from the § 5 tree; `graveyard` writes `graveyard/lessons.json` plus `graveyard/low-confidence/<id>.json` (internal/core/lifeboat/graveyard_lessons.go:161,177), and each ingest fully clears and replaces both. `principles` also writes `principles.md` alongside `principles.json`. `commands/disembark.md:96-98` names the graveyard paths; the brief's own output-shape chapter does not.

discrepancies.claim: § 5 tree: "`rescue/spine.md` — commit-history spine, written where no record store exists".
discrepancies.reality: The condition is the absence of an *intent corpus*, not of a record store. internal/core/lifeboat/plan.go:489 (`// No intent corpus: derive a spine from git history alone`) and sources_native.go:331-344 key it on the intent corpus alone. Demonstrated: a test repo carrying `.abcd/development/decisions/adrs/` and `.abcd/work/issues/` — a record store, with `tiers_present: [git, conventions, abcd-native]` — but no intents still got `rescue/spine.md` written into its lifeboat. The prose one line above (line 90, "the intent corpus where one exists, else the commit history") states the real rule, so the tree comment contradicts its own parent line.

discrepancies.claim: The shipped `probe` sub-verb "run[s] schema/audit checks".
discrepancies.reality: The shipped probe runs a provenance schema-version gate (internal/core/lifeboat/embark.go:202), manifest_sha256 verification, and a symlink/oversize refusal. There is no audit check anywhere in the probe path — the only audit-shaped behaviour in the chapter is `--refresh-audit`, which the same chapter marks as not yet shipped, and a live `disembark pack` now writes `review/**`, not `audit/**`.

discrepancies.claim: `probe` is described only as "show what would land where, run schema/audit checks, write nothing", and its acceptance criterion covers only "file tree, schema validation, would-be writes".
discrepancies.reality: The shipped probe report LEADS with the coverage-blanks handoff — `coverage blanks — answer these first (15 of 23 sections)` plus a per-section question and a `(human-owned — yours to write)` marker (EmbarkPlan.Render / renderCoverageBlanks in internal/core/lifeboat/embark_render.go; `coverage` in the --json payload). It is the first and largest block of real output and commands/embark.md calls it "the point of the handoff", but the chapter's probe bullet and its acceptance criterion never mention it (only the `from` report at §3 step 4 does).

discrepancies.claim: The chapter never mentions `record_manifest_sha256`; grep for "record_manifest"/"record manifest" in the chapter returns nothing.
discrepancies.reality: Both shipped probe surfaces emit it: the human render prints `record manifest sha256: aad33f95…` (embark_render.go) and `--json` carries `record_manifest_sha256` (EmbarkPlan, embark_types.go:219). It is the record-derived closure seal (P1) and is undocumented in this chapter.

discrepancies.claim: "Bucketed families keep their source bucket (issues by state; intents into `drafts`/`planned`/`shipped`/`disciplines`/`superseded`; specs into `open`/`closed`)." — the chapter documents no other bucket behaviour.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped inverse table adds behaviour the chapter omits (internal/core/lifeboat/embark_types.go:292-297, resolveTarget in embark.go:301): a bucket-LESS `rescue/intents/<leaf>` is silently defaulted into `drafts/` (DefaultBucket: "drafts"), while a bucket-less issue or spec has no default and is dropped as Ignored{unmapped} — reported, never written. A bucket-less file alongside its bucketed twin is the `duplicate-target` conflict the chapter names in §2 without explaining where it comes from. The chapter also never names the `unmapped`/`unknown` ignored dispositions the shipped report emits (`ignored (not embarked): 10 report-only, 0 unmapped, 0 unknown`).

discrepancies.claim: "the plain-text `--dry-run` render omits the gate list entirely (it prints only version, files bundled, scan hardfails, citations, and would-publish, plus a would-refuse-on line when there is a finding)" — an explicit closed enumeration of six lines.
discrepancies.reality: `bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 launch --dry-run` prints a seventh, undocumented line: `receipts:       no receipts recorded for a2c77e5; ...`. The renderer emits it at internal/surface/cli/cli.go:298, between `citations:` and `would publish:`. The word "only" makes the enumeration false as written.

discrepancies.claim: The chapter describes the deterministic emit step solely as a mode of `abcd launch ship` ("WITHOUT --changelog-json it runs the EMIT step"); no other verb exposing it is named anywhere in the file.
discrepancies.reality: A shipped top-level verb `abcd changelog` exists (`abcd --help` lists it; internal/surface/cli/ship.go:270-300 `newChangelogCommand`) — a read-only, always-exit-0 preview rendering exactly what `launch ship` emits (derived version, deciding impact, record list, guardrail status). It is named in .abcd/development/brief/04-surfaces/README.md:10 ("the deterministic emit alone is `abcd changelog`") but is absent from 04-launch.md, the chapter README.md defers to for the detail.

discrepancies.claim: Pre-flight gate: "**TruffleHog** — opt-in deep scan when `scan.deep=true` — hard-fail (live credential verification)". No staged/deferred/later-phase marker, unlike the gitleaks bullet above it ("when wired") and the deep smoke tier below ("itd-66, deferred").
discrepancies.reality: No launch path invokes trufflehog. `scanBundle` (internal/core/launch/dryrun.go:110-121) calls `scanner.New` + `sc.ScanBundle` only; there is no deep-scan branch and no `scan.deep` read. `scan.deep` exists solely as an ahoy config slot (internal/core/ahoy/detect.go:174-178, apply.go:374-375). The shipped gate array has six entries — secret+pii-scan, marker-block, installability-smoke, documentation-auditor, citation-baseline, semantic-receipts — none of them a deep scan.

discrepancies.claim: Pre-flight gate: "**Hook compliance** check — warn-fail". Unmarked.
discrepancies.reality: No such gate exists. `abcd launch --dry-run --json` returns exactly six `gates[]` rows and none is hook-compliance; no hook-compliance check exists anywhere under internal/core/launch/. Line 22 of the same file also enumerates "the remaining gates" as exactly two (marker-block, documentation-auditor), which contradicts this bullet's existence.

discrepancies.claim: Pre-flight gate: "**OWASP / vulnerability check** (folded into the pre-flight suite) — warn-fail". Unmarked, and "folded into the pre-flight suite" asserts present wiring.
discrepancies.reality: Nothing vulnerability-shaped runs in the pre-flight suite. The six shipped `gates[]` rows contain no such entry, and `wouldRefuseOn` (internal/core/launch/dryrun.go:143) collects only scan hard-fails, bundle rejections, lockstep drift, retention refusal and smoke findings. `govulncheck` runs as a separate CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml), not as a launch gate.

discrepancies.claim: §5 Bootstrap exception: "the shipped command file covers the read-only dry-run preview and the release cut (emit → compose → ingest)" — a two-flow enumeration of commands/launch.md.
discrepancies.reality: commands/launch.md carries three flows: the dry-run preview, the release cut, and `## Scaffold — the release-gate scaffolder` at commands/launch.md:197, documenting `abcd launch scaffold --json`. (The chapter itself acknowledges this at line 21, "`commands/launch.md` carries the flow", so §5's enumeration is stale against both the file and the chapter.)

discrepancies.claim: First acceptance criterion: bare `/abcd:launch` shows "the available sub-verbs (`ship`, `dry-run`)" — a two-item enumeration of the available sub-verbs.
discrepancies.reality: Three sub-verb surfaces ship: `--dry-run`, `ship`, and `scaffold` (`abcd launch --help` lists `scaffold` and `ship` as Available Commands; the chapter's own Sub-verbs table at lines 14-15 marks `scaffold` shipped). The criterion's enumeration was not updated when itd-93 landed scaffold; the trailing "Design target" note covers the bare-render behaviour, not the stale sub-verb list.

discrepancies.claim: The §2 table row for `/abcd:intent audit <itd-N>` describes the shipped verb as doing the work itself: "Compares the intent's press release + acceptance criteria against delivered reality (code, configs, docs, tests). Per-criterion verdicts (MET / MET_WITH_CONCERNS / NOT_MET / INCONCLUSIVE) appended to the intent's `## Audit Notes`." §7's Role 1 heading repeats the framing ("Compares: intent press release + acceptance criteria / delivered reality"). Neither is marked staged or later-phase.
discrepancies.reality: `abcd intent audit --help` reads "Intent audit (promise vs delivered): re-emit a shipped intent's request, or ingest a verdict". internal/surface/cli/cli.go:1628 wires the bare form to `intent.ReEmitAudit`, which (internal/core/intent/audit.go:26-29, :241) parks an OWED stub in the intent's Audit Notes and writes an ephemeral review request under `.abcd/.work.local/reviews/`. No comparison and no verdict is produced by the verb; only `audit ingest --verdict-json` (IngestVerdict, audit.go:310) writes per-criterion verdicts. The same page states this correctly at :457, so §2 contradicts §7.

discrepancies.claim: "**Bare-command-as-help is a universal abcd convention** — every command in the surface set (the enumeration lives in the surfaces README) shows status + suggested next actions when invoked without args."
discrepancies.reality: Several shipped commands in the surface set render plain cobra help with no status render and no suggested next actions: `abcd docs`, `abcd embark`, `abcd disembark`, `abcd guard` each print only Short + Usage + Available Commands + Flags. (`abcd intent`, `abcd spec`, `abcd capture` do render status, so the convention is real but not universal.)

discrepancies.claim: "The low IDs (itd-1..itd-7) reflect an early one-time rebase to ordering signal. Intents created since are capture-stable, picking up at itd-27+."
discrepancies.reality: The committed intent tree contains itd-8 through itd-26 (19 ids: itd-8..itd-26 all present across drafts/, planned/, shipped/, disciplines/, superseded/ — e.g. itd-16, itd-20, itd-24 in the ranges the chapter itself cites). Capture-stable numbering does not pick up at itd-27; highest id is itd-146.

discrepancies.claim: "**`shipped/`** — a capability built in Go. Empty until the Go build ships capabilities into it (Phase 1 onward)."
discrepancies.reality: `.abcd/development/intents/shipped/` holds 18 intents; `abcd intent` bare status renders "drafts 67 · planned 43 · shipped 18 · disciplines 7 · superseded 4".

discrepancies.claim: "Its `spec_id` is `null` (unscheduled) or points at a `spc-N` once the spec layer schedules it (Phase 4). The native spec store (adr-26) is the scheduling home." — the "(Phase 4)" marker places the spec layer in the future.
discrepancies.reality: The native spec store ships: `abcd spec` is a registered top-level verb, `.abcd/development/specs/{open,closed}/` is populated (open 23 · closed 17), and `abcd intent` bare status renders 41 live itd→spc links (e.g. itd-101 -> spc-17, itd-3 -> spc-1).

discrepancies.claim: "The `/abcd:intent` plugin command surface exists (`commands/intent.md`, resolving iss-105) …"
discrepancies.reality: `commands/intent.md` exists, but iss-105 is still filed in the open bucket: `.abcd/work/issues/open/iss-105-the-intent-verb-family-plan-link-review.md`. The ledger does not record the issue as resolved.

discrepancies.claim: "The shipped record-lint subset is the `intent_lifecycle` rule (the directory/kind/`spec_id` invariants and the `status:`-key ban below), the `intent_impact_valid` rule (the `impact:` field's legal value set), and `persona_registry` … the remaining gates (the `IL0xx` codes …) are plan-time design, a later phase." — a closed three-rule enumeration of what gates the intent tree.
discrepancies.reality: `.abcd/record-lint.json` enables two further blocker rules scoped at the intent tree that the enumeration omits: `record_schema` (`record_stores.itd: .abcd/development/intents`) and `delivery_state` (`intents_root: .abcd/development/intents`).

discrepancies.claim: The block declares "The eight keys below are the canonical seed skeleton the quoted-text create writes" and lists as "Added later, not part of the seed skeleton" exactly three keys: `bundle`, `impact`, `surface_history`. No other intent frontmatter key is documented on this page.
discrepancies.reality: `internal/core/intent/create.go` seedDraft also writes `promoted_from: <iss-N>` — the reciprocal back-edge minted by `abcd capture promote` (spc-24/itd-119). The key is documented in 04-surfaces/06-capture.md but is absent from the intent chapter's canonical frontmatter template and from its "added later" list.

discrepancies.claim: The §2 row for `/abcd:intent ready <itd-N>` states the gate reports "whether an intent is ready to implement — planned, with acceptance criteria and a written spec body" — three checks.
discrepancies.reality: `internal/core/intent/ready.go` runs four checks: planned-bucket, acceptance criteria, `specLinkCheck` (the bidirectional intent↔spec link, ready.go:146-183) and `specBodyCheck`. The bidirectional-link check is missing from the §2 row (the delivery-state note at :3 does list all four).

discrepancies.claim: The frontmatter schema block documents the issue id as `id: iss-N  # unpadded, mirrors itd-N`, and §1/§3 describe an "auto-assigned `iss-N`" allocator writing `iss-N-<slug>.md`.
discrepancies.reality: Shipped ids are 16-digit timestamp-numeric mints, not unpadded sequential ordinals: `internal/core/recordid` mints `<family>-<yymmddHHMMSS><4 random digits>` (recordid tests pin `iss-2608201142070789`), wired into `internal/core/capture/alloc.go:102` (`var minter recordid.Minter`). A live capture in a scratch repo produced `.abcd/work/issues/open/iss-2608231355239205-...md`, and the repo ledger is dual-vintage (`iss-100-...` alongside `iss-2608231346137587-...`). adr-45 ("Record ids are timestamp-numeric") and spc-33 are the governing decisions; the chapter never mentions the mint and its "unpadded, mirrors itd-N" comment is contradicted by every id minted since.

discrepancies.claim: The fast-path row describes `/abcd:capture "<text>"` as appending the free-form text with caller-supplied provenance flags; the chapter documents no processing of the text between input and disk, and §2/§5 list no redaction stage.
discrepancies.reality: Both write paths run the PII/secret scanner over the free text before writing and report what was rewritten. `internal/core/capture/redact.go` (`redactLedgerText`) redacts capture text, slug, found_at and found_during (`workflow.go:59-61`) and the resolution note (`workflow.go:290`), returning a `Redacted` count and a `Degraded` reason that the CLI prints (`internal/surface/cli/cli.go`: "redacted N span(s) before writing…" plus a degraded-scanner WARNING) and that `commands/capture.md` instructs the agent to report. Observed live: `abcd capture "...reading /Users/someone/secret/config..."` printed "redacted 1 span(s)" and wrote `[redacted-path]/secret/config` to the body. The brief chapter documents none of this. (placeholder home path; abcd-lint:allow)

discrepancies.claim: Acceptance criterion 1: "a new file `.abcd/work/issues/open/iss-N-<slug>.md` exists with frontmatter populated and the captured text in the body."
discrepancies.reality: The body holds the *redacted* text, which can differ from the captured text — the scanner rewrites spans before the record is rendered (`redactLedgerText`, `workflow.go:48-61`). Verified: capturing text containing `/Users/someone/secret/config` wrote `[redacted-path]/secret/config` to the body. As written the criterion passes only for text the scanner leaves untouched. (placeholder home path; abcd-lint:allow)

discrepancies.claim: §1 documents only two refusal behaviours under the capture surface — the unfiltered `capture list` exiting 2 (lines 36-40) and `resolve` without `--impact` exiting 1 (line 33). Any other positional input is described as filing an issue.
discrepancies.reality: Two further exit-2 input guards ship and are undocumented in this chapter: a near-miss sub-verb is refused with a did-you-mean rather than filed (`abcd capture resovle iss-1 "x"` → exit 2, `unknown capture subcommand "resovle"; did you mean "resolve"? (nothing captured …)`, `suspectedTypoedSubcommand`, cli.go ~2152), and a lone bare token is read as a sub-verb, never as issue text (`abcd capture nonsenseword` → exit 2, `loneBareToken`, cli.go ~2165); empty text is also refused with exit 2. Both are shipped behaviour (iss-29, iss-2608221328552172) absent from the brief.

discrepancies.claim: "Every bare `spc-38`/`spc-39` on this page is a predecessor-store id cited as provenance — neither id names a spec in this repo's store (`.abcd/development/specs/`), whose own ids stop well short of spc-38."
discrepancies.reality: The repo's spec store has grown past both ids. `.abcd/development/specs/closed/` contains spc-38 (`spc-38-alice-opens-the-record-explorer-and-reads-the-whole-development.md`), spc-39 (`spc-39-maya-sees-how-every-decision-connects.md`) and spc-40 (`spc-40-bob-installs-abcd-with-one-checksum.md`). Both bare ids the page uses ~20 times now collide with live, unrelated in-repo specs, and the disclaimer that was written to prevent that collision is itself false.

discrepancies.claim: `principle-distiller` is an unshipped Phase 6 design target: "The principle-distiller curator role is a Phase 6 design target" (l.56-57); ingest-/ask- run-log trees are "later phase — comes with the principle-distiller curator (Phase 6)" (l.101,104); "`principle-distiller` (design target — Phase 6 ... nothing ships this yet)" (l.118); cost row "Phase 6 design-target agent per 05-internals/01-agents.md, not yet shipped" (l.125).

discrepancies.claim: The Behaviour block lists `abcd update [tag] [--yes] [--json]` and the prose says the verb "resolves the latest, naming the tag before acting" — `--yes` is never explained and no interactive step is described anywhere in the chapter.
discrepancies.reality: internal/surface/cli/update.go gates a bare (no-tag) invocation behind a real TTY confirmation prompt — `resolved latest release: <tag> — proceed? [y/N] ` on stderr, requiring y/yes, otherwise printing `declined — nothing was fetched.` and exiting 0 without fetching. `--yes` is registered as "skip the TTY confirmation of a freshly resolved tag" (visible in `abcd update --help`). The chapter documents neither the prompt, the decline path, nor what `--yes` skips, so a shipped interactive gate on the verb's default form is undocumented.

discrepancies.claim: "every other shape is a loud refusal naming its remedy: a plugin-root binary …, the track-latest dev shim, a stranded owned entry …, a Homebrew Cellar-resolved install …, a foreign occupant, or an empty PATH" — an enumeration of six refusal shapes presented as exhaustive.
discrepancies.reality: The shipped receipt emits eight `refusal.shape` values. Beyond the six listed, internal/core/update/update.go emits `unprovenanced-file` (Apply, when the on-disk target's digest matches no published release — a distinct named refusal with its own remedy, not the same as `foreign`) and `unclassified-target` (Plan's fail-closed default for an unrecognised `ahoy.UpdateTarget` kind). The plugin command commands/update.md does list `unprovenanced-file`; the brief chapter names neither.

discrepancies.claim: "the receipt (origin, tag, digest, old→new) prints in both modes" — the receipt is described as a single shape carrying those four fields, and only two outcomes are implied (a swap, or a refusal).
discrepancies.reality: internal/core/update/update.go defines three actions: `swapped`, `already-current`, and `refused`. The `already-current` outcome (target digest already equals the release's) is never mentioned in the chapter, and its text render prints only `already current: <path> is <tag> (verified against the release checksums)` — no origin, no digest, no old→new. Empirically, a refusal receipt carries none of the four either: `PATH=/nonexistent-dir abcd update --json` returns `{"origin": "", "action": "refused", "refusal": {...}}` with no tag, digest, or versions.

discrepancies.claim: "The bare form is **strictly read-only** … `build` is the render, and it writes only inside the directory it is given," and the Behaviour block describes check as `abcd site check --out DIR  # gate an already-rendered tree`. discrepancies.claim: `abcd site   # what is declared, and what the last build left; exit 0` — the bare form is shown with no flags.
discrepancies.reality: The bare verb carries `--out string` ("output directory to report on", default "site"), per `abcd site --help`, so which directory the read-only render reports on is caller-selectable. The chapter never mentions it.

discrepancies.claim: "the only words the generator may add are the interface strings in `site-src/ui.json`, plus numbers, dates, file names and asset names" — restated in The gates as "matches the allowlist of interface strings, numbers, dates, file and asset names".

The row names only `lint` and characterises the surface as read-only. discrepancies.reality: Thirteen shipped commands with live `commands/*.md` files are absent from this list entirely: docs, history, version, consult, ingest, prepare-this-repo, lint, guard, ideate, identity, banlist, update, site. The caveat covers under-delivery ("not all shipped yet"), not omission — every one of the thirteen has a shipped row in 04-surfaces/README.md and a file in `commands/`.

discrepancies.claim: "The `/abcd:ahoy` slash command dispatches **every** sub-verb (`status | install | uninstall | doctor | dry-run`), the two write verbs included … and each also ships on the CLI as `abcd ahoy <sub-verb>`."

discrepancies.claim: Unmarked present tense: "Each catalog agent declares JSON inputs/outputs (schemas owned by the core, `internal/core/schema`)." The same package is named again at line 90 as the owner of the `task_classes` closed enum.

The brief contradicts itself: 02-constraints/04-naming.md:91 states plainly "This table is the source of truth today: the binary carries no `task_classes` schema and no cross-check test reads the field (iss-265)." Line 3 carries no staged/design-target marker.

discrepancies.claim: The "Agent prompt frontmatter" table enumerates the agents' frontmatter as "Current fields": `name`, `description`, `color`, `prompt_version`, `capability_scope`, `reads_untrusted_input` — followed by an explicit "Deliberately omitted from agent frontmatter" list (`known_failure_modes`, per-task-class `model_id` history, plan-time capability gating output).

discrepancies.claim: "The prompt bodies nonetheless stay **host-agnostic** — no AI vendor or tool name — matching the docs-lint discipline the rest of the surface is held to."
discrepancies.reality: Three shipped prompts name a vendor model. agents/intent-auditor.md:144 embeds `"verifier": { "id": "intent-auditor", "version": "claude-opus-4-8" }` in its worked-example body; agents/ruthless-reviewer.md:5 and agents/security-reviewer.md:5 carry `model: opus`. Four prompts additionally name harness-specific tools in `tools:`. The claim is unenforceable as written: .abcd/docs-lint.json:2 sets `"roots": ["docs", "README.md"]`, so no lint scans agents/ — as the same README paragraph admits. These files are in the shipped bundle (.abcd/config/launch-payload.json includes `agents`), so they reach every install.

discrepancies.claim: "The **Status** column is machine-checked: the `surface_coverage` record-lint rule asserts every `shipped` row has a backing surface (`commands/<name>.md` or `skills/<name>/`) … and, in reverse, that every real surface has a row here. Keeping this column honest is how the brief's surface set stays reconciled with the shipped binary."
discrepancies.reality: The reverse check cannot see the agent surface. `surface_coverage` is configured with `commands_dir: "commands"` and `skills_dir: "skills"` only — there is no `agents_dir` — and `skills_dir` points at a directory that does not exist while `agents/`, which does, is unregistered. `index_drift` (.abcd/record-lint.json:296+) indexes `commands` but has no `agents` index. Yet the binary itself classifies `agents/*.md` as a first-class installed surface: internal/core/launch/installsurface.go:181 registers `SurfaceAgent` over the flat `agents` glob, and it is a required payload directory (payload_completeness_test.go:15). Result: the ten shipped prompt files and the brief's counts of them ("Ten agent prompt files ship in `agents/` today", "Six further agent prompts ship in `agents/` today") are ungated prose — adding, renaming, or deleting a prompt fails no record gate, unlike the equivalent edit under commands/.

discrepancies.claim: The parenthetical documenting the hidden `hook` verb states: "`session-end` is the automatic redact-and-store write path into the transcript store."
discrepancies.reality: `abcd hook session-end` does NOT redact and does NOT write to the store. Binary help: "SessionEnd: stage the raw transcript for the next session to redact and store"; internal/surface/cli/cli.go:1180 calls history.Stage(), writing raw bytes to ~/.abcd/history/<root-sha>/staging/. The redact-and-store write path is `abcd hook session-start` (which drains staging through Capture) — as 04-surfaces/11-history.md:13-20 correctly documents. The README parenthetical is the stale pre-split account (iss-2608230817034768).

discrepancies.claim: "Every event command is a self-provisioning shim, not a plain binary call: the non-SessionStart shims attempt `hooks/bootstrap.sh` when the plugin-root binary is missing (throttled by a `.bootstrap.attempt` marker within a 10-minute window), then fall back to a PATH-resolved `abcd` before failing loudly."
discrepancies.reality: hooks/hooks.json has five event commands; the SessionEnd command contains no reference to bootstrap.sh at all. It is `[ -n "$r" ] || exit 0; if [ -f "$r/abcd" ] && [ -x "$r/abcd" ]; then exec "$r/abcd" hook session-end; fi; if command -v abcd ...` — plugin-root binary, then PATH fallback, then fail loudly. Only three of the four non-SessionStart shims (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PreCompact) self-provision. So "every event command is a self-provisioning shim" is false for SessionEnd.

discrepancies.claim: Tree comment: "hooks/  # Claude Code event hooks — every event command runs through a self-provisioning shim" and "bootstrap.sh  # builds/refreshes the plugin-root binary; referenced by every event command".
discrepancies.reality: The SessionEnd command in hooks/hooks.json never references bootstrap.sh — 4 of the 5 event commands do (UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, PreToolUse, PreCompact). "Every event command" is wrong in both comments.

discrepancies.claim: "The four non-SessionStart event shims also self-provision: when $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/abcd is missing they attempt hooks/bootstrap.sh (throttled by a .bootstrap.attempt marker within a 10-minute window), then fall back to a PATH-resolved abcd before failing loudly."
discrepancies.reality: Only three do. There are four non-SessionStart events (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PreCompact, SessionEnd) but the SessionEnd shim carries no bootstrap.sh attempt and no .bootstrap.attempt marker — verified by parsing hooks/hooks.json: bootstrap.sh present in UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart/PreToolUse/PreCompact, absent from SessionEnd.

discrepancies.claim: `force_refresh_every_n` — "Integer; default 5. Every N prompts, the prompt-router hook forces a full re-inject regardless of dedup signature match (compaction recovery)."
discrepancies.reality: The shipped default is 15: `const DefaultRefreshBackstop = 15` (internal/core/rules/inject.go:31), returned by LoadBackstop for a missing file/key or non-positive value. 05-internals/03-configuration.md:93 correctly says 15; the naming glossary still says 5, so the two brief chapters also contradict each other about the prompt-router hook's own config default.

discrepancies.claim: The chapter narrates the whole session-end capture-budget story (stage-not-redact, why redacting at exit dropped large transcripts) and states the fix means the hook's cost no longer scales with the transcript. No size limit on the staging path is documented anywhere in the brief.
discrepancies.reality: `hook session-end` reads the transcript through fsutil.ReadGuarded with a hard 64 MiB cap (`const maxTranscriptBytes = 64 << 20`, internal/surface/cli/cli.go:1299; readTranscript at :1318). A transcript over the cap returns ErrTooBig, the hook emits a stderr warning and returns nil (exit 0), and the session is permanently lost — the exact failure mode the chapter says was fixed. The cap is an undocumented surface of the session-end entrypoint.

discrepancies.claim: The "Capture promote (spc-30, itd-46 — LIVE)" row states promote is "Skill-orchestrated (lock-acquire → promote-inspect → seed+interview → promote-link → release); never a `capture promote` CLI sub-verb."
discrepancies.reality: abcd ships zero skills (no `skills/` directory in the tree at all), so nothing can be skill-orchestrated; and `abcd capture --help` on the freshly built bin/abcd-darwin-arm64 lists `promote` as a registered CLI sub-verb ("promote — Graduate an issue into an intent draft (mints + stamps promoted_to)"). The named steps `promote-inspect` and `promote-link` are not sub-verbs of `capture` either (its only sub-verbs are list, promote, resolve, wontfix). 04-surfaces/README.md row 6 correctly describes promote as native per spc-24/itd-119, so the matrix contradicts both the binary and the rest of the brief.

discrepancies.claim: "the markdown surfaces (`commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/`) that shell to the binary load cleanly" — names `skills/` as one of the three plugin markdown surface directories.
discrepancies.reality: There is no `skills/` directory in the tree (`ls skills/` → No such file or directory), and it is absent from the release include list in .abcd/config/launch-payload.json. 05-internals/08-skills.md line 48 and 04-surfaces/04-launch.md line 47 both state explicitly that `skills/` does not exist; this build-sequence line still presents it as a loaded surface.

discrepancies.claim: The bare-status-board convention "holds for `ahoy`, `banlist`, `capture`, `memory`, `intent`, `identity`, and `spec` (and bare `abcd`)", with the exceptions named as `version`, `docs`, `history`, `disembark`.
discrepancies.reality: Bare `abcd site` renders a read-only status board (chapters / issue ledger / ui strings / baseline / release / commit / output, then the hint "run `abcd site build` to render") — verified against the built binary. `site` appears on neither side of this enumeration, so a shipped bare-status surface is undocumented in the chapter that defines the convention.
